findings.body:
**Refuse stale `crq-*` units in `--units-output` before preparing the target.**

`prepare` writes only the newly rendered unit files into `--units-output`. It does not remove or reject existing files. `HOST-DEPLOY.md` directs the owner to run `prepare` against the live user manager directory, so a unit that the new target no longer renders, such as `crq-retired.timer`, stays installed after preparation. `unit_sha256` covers only the new files, so the leftover unit is outside the recorded inventory. If its enable link remains, the user manager can start it after `daemon-reload` or login.

Check the output directory for `crq-*` files outside the rendered set and refuse the target until the owner removes them.

```diff
             run(['systemd-analyze', '--user', 'verify', *paths])
+            rendered = {Path(p).name for p in paths}
+            stale = sorted(p.name for p in output.glob('crq-*') if p.name not in rendered) if output.exists() else []
+            if stale:
+                raise ValueError('units output holds crq-* files outside the rendered set: ' + ', '.join(stale))
             record(root, overlay, raw, data, 'prepare', unit_sha256={Path(p).name: digest(Path(p).read_bytes()) for p in paths})
```
findings.title: Refuse stale `crq-` units in `--units-output` before preparing the target.

findings.body:
**Parse the instance through the final unit suffix.**

For `ingress@crq-tick.service.socket` with `Service=%i`, this expression rejects the dotted instance. The scanner leaves `%i` unchanged and detects no dependency. The prefix-filtered listings also omit this socket, so `discover` can return `supported=True`.

Systemd resolves that instance to `crq-tick.service`. Extract everything between the first `@` and the final suffix, or refuse unresolved specifiers. See `unit-live-binding.py:112`. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/systemd/systemd/v255/src/basic/unit-name.c))
findings.title: Parse the instance through the final unit suffix.

findings.body:
**Scan dependency-bearing unit types before accepting the topology.**

An installed `ingress.slice` with `[Unit] Wants=crq-tick.service` is skipped here. Its name also falls outside the manager-listing prefix. With otherwise supported units, `discover` returns `supported=True` despite the foreign activation dependency.

Common `[Unit]` dependencies apply to slice units, and `Wants=` starts the referenced unit. Expand the suffix set or reject unscanned unit types. See `unit-live-binding.py:641-643`. ([freedesktop.org](https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/255/systemd.unit.html))
findings.title: Scan dependency-bearing unit types before accepting the topology.

findings.body:
**Follow-up: suppress cleanup narration in machine mode.**

At `vm-feasibility.py:1231`, a cleanup exception writes to stderr even with `--json`. The cleanup handlers at Line 1129 and Line 1223 have the same defect. Guard these writes with machine-mode state and retain the diagnostic in the JSON result or error.

As per coding guidelines, I1 requires that “in machine mode (`--json`) stderr stays empty.” Based on learnings, defer this Minor finding to a follow-up issue.
findings.title: Follow-up: suppress cleanup narration in machine mode.

findings.body:
**Follow-up: validate report containers before accessing fields.**

At `vm-feasibility.py:347`, `--json verify` with a report containing `[]` raises `AttributeError`. `main()` does not catch that exception, so the command emits a traceback instead of its JSON error artifact. A nonempty list in `image` fails similarly at Line 350.

Validate the report and nested container types before field access. As per coding guidelines, I1 requires exactly one JSON artifact for a machine-mode error. Based on learnings, defer this Minor finding to a follow-up issue.
findings.title: Follow-up: validate report containers before accessing fields.

findings.body:
**Reject undeclared symlink aliases of declared units in `discover`.**

`discover` accepts an undeclared alias such as `ingress.service -> crq-tick.service` without a finding. The entry loop checks only the `crq-tick` prefix (`apps/crq-python/ops/unit-live-binding.py:799`), and no symlink check applies to top-level unit-directory entries. A cotenant `ingress.timer` with `Unit=ingress.service` then produces no match. `Unit` is a scanned directive (`:94-97`), but `CRQ_NAME_RE` (`:93`) requires a `crq-` token, and `ingress.service` has none. The listing and job checks (`:836-861`) filter on the `crq-tick` prefix too. `discover` can therefore return `supported=True` while an unexpected unit activates the selected service through the alias.

Systemd permits a plain unit to be aliased by a plain name of the same type, and aliases can be used in unit dependency directives ([freedesktop.org](https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/255/systemd.unit.html)). Reject undeclared aliases that resolve to a declared unit:

<details>
<summary>Suggested fix</summary>

```diff
         declared_set = {str(path) for path in declared}
+        declared_resolved = set()
+        for path in declared:
+            try:
+                declared_resolved.add(path.resolve())
+            except (OSError, RuntimeError):
+                declared_resolved.add(path)
         prefix = unit.split(".")[0]
         for entry in sorted(entries):
             name = entry.name
@@
                 if dropin_error is not None:
                     foreign.append(dropin_error)
                 continue
+            if entry.is_symlink() and str(entry) not in declared_set:
+                try:
+                    alias_target = entry.resolve(strict=False)
+                except (OSError, RuntimeError):
+                    alias_target = None
+                if alias_target in declared_resolved:
+                    foreign.append("undeclared alias of a declared unit: "
+                                   + str(entry))
+                    continue
             if name.startswith(prefix) and str(entry) not in declared_set:
                 foreign.append("unexpected installed entry: " + str(entry))
```

</details>
findings.title: Reject undeclared symlink aliases of declared units in `discover`.

findings.body:
**Give each download invocation its own `.part` file.**

`download` writes every invocation to the same `<name>.part` path and opens it with `"wb"`, which truncates it. Two invocations that share a state directory and start with an empty image cache can therefore write the same file. The second invocation can truncate bytes that the first has not yet verified. The first invocation then either fails its digest check or renames a file that the other invocation is still writing into the cache. Use a per-invocation temporary name so each download verifies and renames only its own file.

<details>
<summary>Suggested fix</summary>

```diff
 def download(url: str, destination: pathlib.Path, timeout: float = 120) -> str:
     """Download to a sibling ``.part`` and fsync before replacing."""
-    part = destination.with_name(destination.name + ".part")
+    part = destination.with_name(f"{destination.name}.{uuid.uuid4().hex}.part")
```

</details>
findings.title: Give each download invocation its own `.part` file.

findings.body:
**Stop the run-named scope when `process.json` is missing.**

When `process.json` is absent, `stop_owned_process` sets `stopped = True` at `vm-feasibility.py:1261` and skips all process checks. `boot()` spawns QEMU before it writes `process.json`. The `recorder.append` at line 586 runs before the `try`, and the pid-file wait can run for up to 30 seconds. A failure or interruption in that window leaves a running guest with no recorded identity. `destroy` then reports `stopped: true`. With `--purge`, it also moves the overlay, seed, and SSH credentials of the live guest.

The scope name is derived from `run_id`, so the stop does not need the identity file. Stop that unit, and report `stopped` only after `systemctl is-active` shows it inactive. This also covers the failure cleanup in `cmd_boot`, which calls this function.

<details>
<summary>Suggested fix</summary>

```diff
     needle = str(run_dir / "overlay.qcow2")
     stopped = True
     stop_rc = None
+    if identity is None:
+        derived_unit = "crq-vm-" + run["run_id"] + ".scope"
+        stop_rc = subprocess.run(["systemctl", "--user", "stop", derived_unit],
+                                 capture_output=True, text=True).returncode
+        stopped = subprocess.run(["systemctl", "--user", "is-active", "--quiet",
+                                  derived_unit]).returncode != 0
     if identity is not None:
```

</details>
findings.title: Stop the run-named scope when `process.json` is missing.
